h1: LK President Pattaya — a roomy 4-star LK hotel in central Pattaya
intro: If you want a 4-star hotel in central Pattaya with spacious, good-value rooms within walking distance of the beach and night markets, yet far enough back from the chaos of Walking Street to actually sleep — LK President, part of the LK Group and opened in 2015 on Pattaya 3rd Road, is a name a lot of people bring up · the rooms are spacious with marble floors and private balconies, and there's a pool, gym, sauna and an in-house restaurant · it's about a 10–15 min walk to Pattaya Beach, close to Tree Town market and the Night Bazaar · from around THB 1,400/night on weekdays · scored 8.6 from thousands of real reviews.

body.html: Who LK President is for — if we had to sum it up in one line, LK President is a 4-star hotel for anyone who wants a "big room at an affordable price" in central Pattaya, without paying beachfront-resort money · the hotel belongs to the LK Group, a large local hotel chain with several properties scattered across Pattaya, so it's a familiar name to frequent Pattaya visitors · it's been open since 2015 and sits on Pattaya 3rd Road, one block back from the beach road — close enough to walk to the beach and the eating-and-nightlife spots, but pulled back far enough from the din of the beachfront strip · real reviews agree on who fits in here: value-focused travellers, couples or groups of friends on a short Pattaya trip, and families who want a room big enough for an extra bed or kids · at the same time we should be straight about it: this is not a designer boutique hotel or a luxury beachfront resort, so anyone expecting a flawless brand-new room in every corner or genuinely five-star service may need to adjust their expectations — LK President's selling point is "space and location at this price" rather than luxury · the hotel is still operating normally and remains a popular pick among Pattaya's budget-to-midrange hotels.

Location and getting around — LK President sits on Pattaya 3rd Road in Nongprue, Bang Lamung, a central Pattaya area one block back from the beach · the strength of this location is "close but not too close" — about a 10–15 min walk gets you to Pattaya Beach and the beach road, while at night you don't get the full blast of beach-road noise the way the seafront hotels do · within walking distance there's plenty to eat and explore: the Tree Town night market is about 400 metres away and Pattaya Night Bazaar about 700 metres, both an easy stroll · for Walking Street, it's about 2 km — a quick motorbike taxi or songthaew ride · big malls like CentralFestival Pattaya Beach and Terminal 21 are a short drive away too · a bit further out, Jomtien Beach is about 5 km, U-Tapao Airport is about a 40 min drive, and from Bangkok via the motorway it's roughly an hour and a half to two hours · one small note: Pattaya 3rd Road gets fairly busy in the evenings, and some stretches of pavement aren't that even, so take a little care walking at night.

"The room was bigger than I expected for the price — marble floors and a balcony you can actually sit on · about ten minutes' walk to the beach, and coming back to sleep it's a lot quieter than the hotels on the beach road. The night market is right behind the hotel, so you can just walk over to eat."

Room types and decor — the thing LK President gets talked about most is room size · many reviews agree the rooms here are noticeably bigger than similarly priced hotels in Pattaya · the entry-level rooms like the Deluxe King and Deluxe Twin have marble floors that feel airy and easy to clean, plus a balcony or private terrace, fridge, minibar, safe and a flat-screen TV with satellite channels · step up to the One Bedroom Suite, which separates the living room from the bedroom — good for longer stays or anyone who wants extra lounge space · and the largest is the Two Bedroom Family Suite, for families or groups of friends travelling together · the decor is the warm, classic style of the LK chain rather than sleek modern minimalism — if you prefer a clean, modern look, some details may feel a bit dated · one point that shows up in reviews is that the furniture and fittings in some rooms are starting to show their age, and room quality is fairly inconsistent — some rooms look newer and better kept than others · the tip from many guests is that if you get a room you're not happy with, ask the front desk to change it, because the hotel has plenty of rooms and is usually flexible.

Facilities, pool and gym — LK President has the standard facilities you'd expect from a city hotel · there's an outdoor pool for a cooling dip after a full day of walking around, a gym with a reasonable amount of equipment, and a sauna for anyone who wants to unwind · we should be honest, as the real reviews reflect, that the pool here is not large — it's more for a cooling dip than for serious lap-swimming, and at times the pool and sauna look a bit aged, with some grumbles about maintenance · for extra services there's an in-house restaurant with room service, free parking (a plus for anyone driving down from Bangkok), airport transfers for an extra charge, luggage storage and laundry · Wi-Fi is where opinions split — some reviews say it works fine, but plenty of others complain it's slow or unstable in certain rooms, especially the ones far from the access points · anyone who needs to work online seriously should have a mobile SIM as a backup plan.

Food and the in-house restaurant — the hotel has an in-house restaurant serving breakfast and other meals · breakfast is a buffet, generally open in the morning from around 7 to 11 · reviews on breakfast are fairly middle-of-the-road — there's a decent range of both Thai and international options, but some say the flavours are plain and ordinary, the kind of breakfast that "fills you up, don't expect much" · what helps a lot is the hotel's location, because it's surrounded by roadside eateries, seafood spots and night markets within easy walking distance, so many people choose to eat out rather than have every meal in the hotel — which is part of the appeal of staying in central Pattaya · the nearby Tree Town market and Night Bazaar have street food, desserts and drinks to try in the evening · overall, food isn't a reason to come for the in-house dining at LK President, but it's a decent add-on, and the location more than makes up for it with options outside.

Service — service is a point that earns fairly consistent praise in the real reviews · many front-desk staff are described as friendly, helpful and able to communicate in English, which makes for a smooth stay for international guests · check-in and check-out are quick, with few problems with long queues · staff also help with calling cars, recommending places to go, and are flexible about room changes when guests aren't happy with their original room · but to be straight, some reviews say the standard of cleaning and housekeeping is inconsistent — some rooms are spotless, while others have spots the housekeeping didn't get to in detail, especially the bathrooms · a few people also note that some staff members' English isn't yet fluent · overall, service is still good for a hotel in this price range, and the team's friendliness goes a fair way toward covering the other shortcomings.

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — gathered from Trip.com, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: spacious, good-value rooms are mentioned most, marble floors and private balconies feel airy and comfortable, the central Pattaya location is walkable to the beach and night markets, staff are friendly and speak English, free parking, and good overall value within the same price bracket · on the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is noise — even pulled back from the beach road, some rooms facing the nearby bars still pick up loud music into the small hours, sometimes until 4 a.m. on weekend nights · next is furniture and some rooms starting to age with the building (a few mention cigarette burns on old furniture), Wi-Fi that's slow or unstable in some rooms, air-conditioning that drips or doesn't get cold enough in some rooms, inconsistent bathroom cleanliness, and the aged-looking pool and sauna · most of these complaints can be eased by choosing the right room and setting your expectations correctly, rather than being big enough to keep people from coming back.

"Great value for the price — big room, lovely staff · the only downside was the Saturday night music from the bars nearby carrying on late. Next time I'll ask for an inside-facing room that doesn't look out onto the street, and it should be just right."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Deluxe room is around THB 1,400/night at the normal weekday rate, rising to roughly THB 2,000–2,800 on weekends or in high season · suites like the One Bedroom and Two Bedroom Family Suite run from around THB 2,500 up, depending on size and season · compared with hotels of the same level in central Pattaya, LK President's selling point is that you get a bigger room for the same budget, which is great value for families or groups of friends who need the space · against newer chain hotels in the same area like Holiday Inn Express or ibis, whose rooms are smaller but newer and more consistent — LK President wins on space and price, but loses on newness and room consistency · the simple takeaway: if you weight "room space per baht" and a central location, this place is great value, but if you weight a spotless new room and modern design, there may be a better fit in a similar budget.

Things to know before booking — a few things make for a smoother stay · one, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask at booking or check-in for an inside-facing room that doesn't look out onto the street or toward the bars, because weekend nights get loud late · two, room quality is fairly inconsistent — if you get a room you're not happy with, ask the front desk to change it; the hotel has plenty of rooms and is usually flexible · three, if you need the internet for serious work, bring a mobile SIM as backup, since Wi-Fi is slow in some rooms · four, if you're driving yourself you're at an advantage, with free parking that's hard to find in central Pattaya · five, check whether breakfast is included in the room rate when you book, since some platforms offer both included and not-included rates · six, on long weekends Pattaya gets crowded and prices climb fast, so book ahead and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't set.

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, LK President is the best fit for anyone who wants a spacious, good-value room in central Pattaya, within walking distance of the beach and night markets, without paying a lot · the bigger-than-the-competition room for the same budget, a location that's close but not too rowdy, friendly staff and free parking make it a value pick among Pattaya's budget-to-midrange hotels · but you have to accept this is a building that's been open since 2015, so there are details starting to age, room quality is inconsistent, Wi-Fi is slow in some rooms, and weekend nights bring noise from the nearby bars · if you're after a flawless brand-new room, modern design or five-star service, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a newer chain hotel or a beachfront resort instead · but for a Pattaya trip where you mainly want plenty of room space, a central location and value — LK President fits that group's needs well, and it's why it still earns good review scores from thousands of real guests.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — LK President Pattaya

faq.q: Where is LK President Pattaya, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: The hotel is on Pattaya 3rd Road in Nongprue, central Pattaya · it's about a 10–15 min walk to Pattaya Beach · the Tree Town night market is about 400 metres away and Pattaya Night Bazaar about 700 metres, both walkable · Walking Street is about 2 km, a short ride, while CentralFestival is about a 10 min drive.

faq.q: What chain is LK President, and how many stars?
faq.a: LK President is a 4-star hotel in the LK Group, a large local hotel chain with several properties across Pattaya · it's been open since 2015 · it's a familiar name to frequent Pattaya visitors among the budget-to-midrange hotels.

faq.q: What's the starting price at LK President, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,400/night for a Deluxe King or Deluxe Twin on weekdays · there's a One Bedroom Suite and a Two Bedroom Family Suite for families or groups of friends · weekend and high-season prices climb fast, so compare several platforms before booking.

It's a great fit for anyone who wants a spacious, good-value room in central Pattaya — couples, groups of friends and families who need plenty of room space · its strength is rooms bigger than the competition for the same budget and a location within walking distance of the beach · if you're after a flawless brand-new room with modern design or a beachfront resort, another option may suit you better.

faq.q: What's the noise like at LK President, and which room should I ask for?
faq.a: Even though the hotel is pulled back from the beach road, weekend nights still bring music from nearby bars carrying on late in street-facing rooms · if you're a light sleeper, ask for an inside-facing room that doesn't look out onto the street right from booking or check-in.

faq.q: Does LK President have a pool and parking?
faq.a: There's an outdoor pool (not large, more for a cooling dip) plus a gym and sauna on site · and there's free parking that's hard to find in central Pattaya, ideal for anyone driving down from Bangkok · breakfast is a buffet — check whether it's included in the room rate when you book.
